title: Punt FT%: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt FT% build in our 12-team H2H 9-cat league, and how should they be tiered by auction value? Each line must also note the guard stats (AST, 3PTM, ST, PTS) a player brings, because the experts warn that drafting only bad free throw shooters punts four categories.
summary: A punt FT% build in our league usually starts with Giannis. It only works if you keep buying assists, threes, steals and points next to him. The players below fit the punt, but none of them is credited with real three-point volume, so you have to find threes outside this list. Do not overbid on bad free throw shooters just because punt rankings like them.

paragraphs.text: Free throws are linked to points, threes and assists. If you draft only bad free throw shooters, you are really punting four categories, not one. In our 9-cat H2H format that hands an opponent four categories every week before the games start.

The fix is the same in every note. If you open with a bad free throw shooter like Giannis, punt FT% but get assists, threes and steals early. You do not need to chase low free throw players. Your targets are still every player in the pool.

sections.heading: Experts disagree: does Giannis force the punt?

paragraphs.text: One view treats Giannis as the anchor of a punt FT% team that also gives up TO, carried by his FG%, points, rebounds and frontcourt assists. The other view says taking Giannis in round one does not mean you have to punt free throws or target other bad free throw shooters. In practice, buy Giannis for his strengths. Then decide on the punt only after you see which players come cheap in the auction.

The experts say to draft guards in two of the next three rounds after punting a guard stat. In our auction, that means two of your next three buys after Giannis should be players who bring assists, threes or steals. Otherwise you slide into a 4 or 5 category punt.

Do not push up the price of players who gain value in punt rankings just to secure them. Bad FT% players are the usual example. Set a ceiling for each one before October 18 and let him go if the bidding passes it. Other managers rarely chase these players, so many of them stay cheap.

Overall 9-cat ranks can mislead you here. If you punt FT, a drop in a player's FT% barely matters to you, even if his overall rank falls a lot. Judge each target only on the eight categories you are still trying to win.

Free throws are the most variable fantasy category. Do not decide to punt based on one bad season, because FT% swings both ways. When you buy a poor shooter, price him as if his free throws will stay bad, and treat any improvement as a bonus. Mobley and Banchero are the players to watch here. Their notes ask you to check whether Mobley's FT% recovers and whether Banchero stays near last season's 77.5%.

A poor free throw shooter who starts the game is partly protected from hack-a-player tactics, because there are no team fouls early in the game. That makes starting centers like Gobert, Claxton and Nurkic safer buys than bench bigs.

sections.heading: Where the guard stats come from

paragraphs.text: For steals, look at Daniels (about 2.2 per game projected), Ausar Thompson (elite steals) and Pippen (about 1.8). For assists, look at Castle (7.3 projected), Sengun (assists from the center spot) and Nurkic. Barnes and Giannis add frontcourt assists. For points, the notes credit Giannis, Zion (22 to 23), Banchero and Siakam.

None of these players is credited with three-point volume. Barnes fell to 0.8 threes per game. Daniels and Ausar fit punt 3PM builds, and Kessler gives few threes. So you need to buy threes from good free throw shooters outside this list, or you are punting both shooting categories.

Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28. Sengun has only 10 games in that stretch. Siakam plays 3-4-3. Mobley has a two-game finals week, and Minnesota has a two-game week in week 20. Boston has three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks, which hurts Robinson if he sits them. Use these as tiebreakers when two targets are close in price.
